title: Book Endorsements
intro: Words about the Empowerment Therapy book.
empty_message: Book endorsements will be added soon.

items.quote:
I wish I had had this wonderful book earlier in my career as the director of the Psychological Services Center at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign, where we trained future generations of therapists and community practitioners. It is written with Myra’s signature clarity, wisdom, humor, humility and authenticity – and will be a valuable addition to the learning libraries of both beginner and seasoned practitioners.

The focus on “needs” increased effectiveness and inspired more creative solutions in response to client concerns. The “needs-based empathy” allowed therapists to uncover additional layers of meaning and depth with greater ease and speed. Finally, through its emphasis on connection, the needs-based approach improved the therapeutic alliance.
items.author: Elaine Shpungin, Ph.D., founder and Director of Conflict 180 and former Director of the Psychological Services Center at the University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

items.quote: With clarity and practical examples, Myra walks us through Empowerment Therapy while bringing to light the power and potential for healing that it holds. Through Myra’s personal and professional experiences, we have an opportunity not only to learn theory, but to apply the concepts directly into the fabric of our lives and the lives of clients. Myra’s book is a delightful and essential resource.
items.author: Kathleen Macferran, author of Choice: A Field Guide for Navigating the Polarization of Our World and Living Interdependently

items.quote: Myra Walden is inviting you to join her on an adventure that may deepen your practice, enrich your relationships and increase intimacy and connection in your personal and professional lives. Nonviolent Communication is a seemingly simple tool that is able when employed to make remarkable changes in understanding and empathy. Myra is an exquisite teacher who maps this path and brings you along in her joyful celebration of this effective practice. Be prepared for the possibilities this powerful tool can bring into your life, practice and network.
items.author: Shelley Reither, MA

items.quote:
Had I read Myra’s book decades ago, I would not have ended up with burnout, after a 12-year psychotherapy practice. I would have been aware of the necessity for caring for my own needs. And I believe I would have been much more able to meet my clients where they were at, and help them embrace and heal their pain. So, in a way this book stimulates some sadness and regret in me.

At the same time, I am very happy that this book is available, hoping that many, many psychotherapists will study it, and be inspired and encouraged to implement the model in their therapy practice. What is needed in order to put it in practice is not merely cognitive understanding, but transformative learning in which the student, in our case the psychotherapist, exposes themselves to a journey of genuine inner transformation.
items.author: Robert Maoz Kržišnik, MSc, Psych (Slovenia, EU), author of This Miraculous Life

items.quote: Since I took a weekend NVC training with Myra Walden in 2008, my ability to work with high conflict couples has significantly improved. The training offered me an opportunity to develop not only a set of skills, but even more importantly, an understanding of the healing power that lies in unearthing and validating people’s unacknowledged needs. There is no question that this training has been instrumental in my growth as a therapist, as well as in my own personal relationships.
items.author: Ann Randolph, MS, LCPC

items.quote: I use the principles of NVC with virtually every client I see. With parents and children, the needs provide a language that is clear, useful, and blame-free. Conflicts can then be seen in a far more neutral light and can be resolved without coercion or damage to relationships. Adolescents and adults learn to use the needs to explore and validate what is inside. Needs are immensely helpful in making decisions, resolving ambivalence, and sorting out relationship problems. In addition, I see that working with the needs promotes self-esteem, resilience, and healthy responsibility.
items.author: Ellen M. Keating, PsyD
